review: Weird and smart and interconnected in all the best ways

I played all four episodes of The Lion Song, and while I would say none were as good as the first episode, as a whole the game was an enjoyable visual novel to progress through so long as you're not expecting much. Art style was nice pixel art, though the sepia did get rather boring after a while.

Well worth giving the first episode a try for free, and then wait for the other episodes on sale if they piqued your interest enough.

This is less a game, than a wonderful story! A story about art, progress, emancipation, diversity and the consequences of our words and actions. It's very touching and deep, a love letter to artworks, which became an artwork by itself!
I disagree a lot with some toxic reviews here, that it would be only about a "horny woman", because this statement's wrong for many reasons. For example (best example) that it's not only about one woman, it's about many people (protagonists are changing depending on the episode).
Like I've mentioned before, the whole main focus here is the story. The few gameplay elements are the possibility to make choices and to observe your surroundings.
4 hours only may seem short, but keep in mind that I'm still missing 45 more achievements of 86 in total!
So yes, I can recommend it a lot and wish to give you a small advice how to save money: you should not only wait until it's in discount, you should buy it then as a bundle!

Сразу скажу, что для меня Львиная песнь стала шедевром и знаковым произведением, которое навсегда останется со мной. Играть за представителей интеллигенции и искусства в сеттинге Австро-Венгрии начала 20 века, в Прекрасной эпохе, до той ужасной войны - это то, чего я так хотела, сама о том не зная. Мое знакомство с этой игрой - удача и огромное счастье.
Эта игра - ода человеческому разуму и силе духа! Безумно жизнеутверждающее произведение, которое показывает, что прекрасная, сияющая, созидательная сущность Человека будет жива всегда. Она бессмертна, она всегда пробьется, словно цветок сквозь асфальт, и ее не растопчет никакая война своими грязными сапогами. Никогда.
Игра вызвала катарсис и натолкнула на размышления. Это все, что мне нужно от произведения искусства. А эта игра им является вне всяких сомнений. Графика приятная, со вкусом сделана. Музыка только там, где она нужна, чтобы подчеркнуть какой-то поворот сюжета. Заглавная композиция улетела в плейлист, такая она светлая, возвышенная и безумно сильная. Она идеально отражает сам дух этой игры. Главные персонажи - живые, с упрямым разумом и тонкой душой. Некоторые второстепенные обозначены лишь парой штрихов, но они тоже безумно живые и настоящие.
Я не думаю, что эта игра зайдет всем. Она на свою аудиторию. Однако я все равно рекомендую ее всем, ибо если она вам понравится, то есть шанс, что она что-то изменит в вас, как изменила во мне. Дух прекрасной Австро-Венгрии с ее сияющей Веной - колыбелью искусства, науки, психоанализа - не отпускает меня, и я отправляюсь читать "Вчерашний мир" Стефана Цвейга. Спасибо Львиной песне за то, что вдохновила меня и дала прочувствовать дух этой навсегда ушедшей Прекрасной эпохи. Красивая, пронзительная, очень умная, замечательная игра.

[h2]Review for Episode 1: Silence[/h2]
First of all, I really like the pixelart. The reduced color palette reminds me of old photopgraphs which fits the time the story is set in. It's great to see a story about a female composer and her struggles without putting her in the spotlight as a woman but rather as an artist. Female composers faced hardships at that time (and they still do) and it's important to keep that in mind, at the same time it's great this story doesn't reduce her to being a woman. Portraying her as the artist she is, with all her flaws, dreams and struggles was heart-warming and I felt like this could've been a real story of an actual person. After your first playthrough you can see the percentage of other players who made the same major decisions as yourself which was really cool. You are also given the opportunity to jump back into the story right before every decision to change it and see the outcome which was not only great for getting some achievements but generally a really nice quality of life feature for people who want to see different paths of the story. The music was great, too, I really enjoyed the final song. Getting all achievements was a little tedious since you need to play through the game several times, but overall not hard, it took me less than 2.5 hours. I'm excited to play the other episodes, too.

Gioco che ricorda molto la struttura antologica del film Cloud Atlas: vari episodi ciascuno con un proprio protagonista ma dove alla fine ci si accorge che ogni gesto compiuto da ciascuno di loro ha ripercussioni sull'esistenza di tutti gli altri. Il gameplay è molto semplice; nonostante il sistema punta e clicca, siamo di fatto ai limiti della visual-novel. Quindi si basa tutto su scelte-conseguenze e non solo in forma di dialogo, ma anche tramite l'interazione con oggetti o come affrontare certi enigmi (incluso l'insuccesso nella risoluzione). Anche l'aspetto estetico è molto semplice con un pixellato non buonissimo ma che è reso accattivante dalla colorazione a poche tonalità cromatiche e dalla musica maliconica e angosciante. 
Infine è affascinante l'ambientazione viennese della bell'epoque caratterizzata da una sospensione tra modernità del 900 e arcaicismi dell'ormai decadente impero asburgico. 
Il vero difetto è nella differenza di peso tra i vari episodi. L'unico che sembra essere sufficientemente ricco sotto ogni punto di vista, scrittura, gameplay, impatto e via dicendo, sembra essere il terzo. Al confronto il secondo sembra affrettato e il primo e il secondo, semplicemente prologo ed epilogo che veri episodi.
Comunque l'impatto emotivo che il gioco riesce a creare e la sua alta rigiocabilità bastano a compensare tali difetti e a consigliarlo.

Como las historias se construyen de a poco al inicio, con referencias a otros personajes, y luego ver a los anteriores en el futuro... Como concluyen todas las historias en el epílogo... ES VERDADERAMENTE INCREÍBLE Y... Triste... todo inició y terminó bien, hasta la fatídica conclusión del capítulo 4...

Hay juegos que se quedan en la memoria del jugador, ya sea por sus historias, los personajes entrañables, la jugabilidad o el arte. Para el jugador que escribe esto, La Canción del León sonara tanto tiempo como estancia en este mundo sea posible. Y al final, al igual que mis abuelos, me encargaré de contar las buenas historias a quienes estén dispuestos a escucharlas.

Jeu d'aventure narratif à choix multiples, The Lion's Song nous fait vivre à travers 4 chapitres l'histoire de trois personnages principaux :
- Une jeune compositrice en recherche d'inspiration dans les Alpes
- Un jeu peinture qui cherche à affiner son style à travers de nouveaux modèles
- Une mathématicienne qui combat pour justifier sa place dans un monde d'élites masculines

Les trois personnages de croisent de façon indirecte, la force du jeu étant sa (très bonne) qualité d'écriture.

Le style "sépia" des graphismes passe bien, donnant un côté ancien dans cette Vienne des années 1910, d'avant guerre.

今天把apex通行证打通了。忽然丧失了游玩欲望。下了一堆新游戏不知如何下手。加上今天一整天没课遂选了重新打开the lion’s song。真得很震撼。淡黄色的古朴画面如画卷般在眼前展开，存在感微弱的音乐却让人慢慢沉静下来。这是一部需要细听、细玩的游戏。在数学家的终章里，女数学家EM和质疑她理论和性别的大学教授在满课堂的学生面前当堂对峙，那时仅仅是随情绪和时机跳动的文字，配上悠扬变化的古典乐便让我心为之颤动。玩完这一章后，我的心情久久不能平复，因为我感到了胸中真正的愉悦。我觉得自己曾经可能也有过这种感受，比如看完一场真正的好电影。不敢继续再玩下去，害怕以后再找不到这么优美的视觉小说游戏了。想要找代餐，却一直没能如愿。有的游戏剧情虽精彩却缺少了伟大的深意，有的游戏制作精良却因为玩法过于复杂而错失了与心灵交汇的机会。我真的好害怕，这款游戏让我对其它的同类游戏抱有了太强的期待，以至于一直不能满足。但我并不后悔它让我玩它。

The Lion’s Song é uma obra-prima de narrativa interativa que se destaca por sua originalidade e profundidade emocional. Desenvolvido pela Mi'pu'mi Games, este jogo independente oferece uma experiência verdadeiramente imersiva ao explorar temas profundos como criatividade, inspiração e as complexidades das relações humanas.

Um dos maiores pontos fortes do jogo é sua estética única. A escolha por uma arte em píxel art monocromática não só contribui para um clima nostálgico, mas também complementa perfeitamente a atmosfera introspetiva e melancólica da narrativa. O estilo visual minimalista, aliado à trilha sonora delicada, cria uma sensação de intimidade que captura o jogador desde o início.

A estrutura episódica do jogo permite que cada capítulo seja dedicado a personagens e temas diferentes, mas que se intercetam de maneira significativa. Cada episódio mergulha no processo criativo e nas lutas internas dos protagonistas, seja uma compositora em busca de inspiração, um matemático lidando com questões de identidade ou uma pintora tentando capturar a essência dos seus modelos. Essas histórias são profundamente humanas, explorando temas como o perfecionismo, as pressões sociais e a busca pela autenticidade artística.

Além disso, The Lion’s Song incentiva a reflexão através das suas escolhas narrativas. As decisões feitas ao longo do jogo não apenas afetam o desenvolvimento imediato da história, mas também têm repercussões em capítulos subsequentes. Isso cria um senso de agência no jogador, reforçando a ideia de que pequenas decisões podem ter grandes impactos, tanto na vida dos personagens quanto no próprio rumo da narrativa.

Outro aspeto notável é como o jogo aborda questões culturais e sociais do início do século XX, incluindo o papel das mulheres nas artes e nas ciências numa época dominada por homens. O jogo equilibra perfeitamente a discussão dessas questões com a exploração dos conflitos internos dos personagens, tornando-o relevante tanto em termos históricos quanto emocionais.

No geral, The Lion’s Song é uma obra rica, que transcende o género de aventura narrativa ao proporcionar uma experiência meditativa e envolvente. A combinação de uma narrativa bem escrita, visuais cativantes e uma trilha sonora comovente faz dele uma obra de arte interativa inesquecível.

The Lion's Song is an absolute delight to play, brilliantly weaving together episodes that captivate and challenge players to think deeply about the clues presented. Each story is beautifully interconnected, adding layers of complexity and intrigue that keep you engaged throughout the game.

One standout moment is the powerful debate between Emma and Zahler. This exchange showcases her tenacity and intellect as she proves her groundbreaking theory on the elements of change. It's a powerful and inspiring moment that truly resonates. Being directly involved in those decisions is fun.

This game is a must-play for those who appreciate thought-provoking narratives and masterfully crafted storytelling. The Lion's Song is a rare gem that will leave you reflecting on its memorable characters and connections long after you've finished playing.

Mit eindeutiger, aber keinesfalls aufdringlicher Dramatik wird in "The Lion´s Song" im Wien der Belle Epoque wiedererweckt in den ersten drei Episoden. In der vierten Episode wird einem dann vor allem klar was für eine herausragende kulturelle Blüte mit dem Ersten Weltkrieg dort begann zu vergehen. 
Viel zu Rätseln gibt es in "The Lion´s Song"  nicht.  Das Spiel entspinnt sich über die eigenen Handlungen im Spiel. Die spielen sich dann weitestgehend im dialogischen ab. Auch wenn die ersten drei Episoden weitestgehend unabhängig voneinander wirken, wird bei einem zweiten Durchspielen erst deutlich, wie fein die Verwebungen an den Berührungspunkten der einzelnen Episoden sind. 
Die zweifelnde Musikerin, der getrieben Maler und die ehrgeizige Mathematikerin scheinen erst einmal nur Figuren ihrer Episoden zu sein, doch in der vierten Episode gelingt etwas, was in Spielen nicht allzu oft gelingt. Mit einem vorbereiteten einfachen und dennoch eleganten Kniff zeigt sich wie die Leben dieser drei Figuren auf andere Ausstrahlen. Das passiert nicht im simplen Zeigen einer Ursache, diesen Protagonisten wird dabei auch Tiefe zugestanden. Das Wien vom Vorabend des Ersten Weltkriegs beschränkt sich damit nicht nur auf schillernde Persönlichkeiten. Es wird auch die Stadt selbst gezeigt. 
So ist "The Lion´s Song" ein einfühlsames Portrait von Menschen, die ihre Stadt ausmachen und auch das Stille Portrait einer Stadt. Nicht jede Facette städtischen Lebens wurde damit abgedeckt, natürlich. Nur schafft es "The Lion´s Song" eine Vorstellung von Boheme und Leben in Wien vor dem Jahr 1914 zu vermitteln. Die Ambitionen, die in diesen Spiel stecken, konnte vom Entwicklerteam jedenfalls eingelöst werden. Die Sepiaoptik unterstreicht dabei den nostalgischen Faktor einer vergangenen Zeit.
Für das Spielen ist derweil nicht mehr notwendig als das grundlegende Geschick eine PC-Maus benutzen zu können. Womit sich glücklicher Weise nicht Raffinesse aufgeladen wird, die dem Vergnügen vor allem abträglich und nicht zuträglich ist.
Es ist zu besseren Vergnügen geraten mehr den Figuren als der Handlung zu folgen. Und wie oben bereits erwähnt ist ein zweiter Durchgang wirklich zu empfehlen.

[u]Praises[/u]
    • Creative pixel art.
    • Interactive credits.

    • Demonstrates negative intrusive thoughts really well (Episode 1). I, too, have internally screamed for them to stop before. 
    • Sexist mathematicians getting served (Episode 3).
    • Criticisms of war (Episode 4). 

[u]Complaints[/u]
    • Points of view jump around in unhelpful ways. 
    • I just couldn’t give enough sh*ts about the characters.
    • Gameplay is boring, which is a big negative considering games are supposed to be entertaining. 

I feel like this is an unpopular opinion considering how many positive reviews this game has, but I don’t particularly recommend this game and I just couldn’t get into it. The short stories themselves are fine, but their execution is just tedious and boring. 
Yo, I like achievements and all, but they’re really excessive in this game and the player has to play through the episodes 2-4 times to get them all. There is a “decide again” feature that allows you to change decisions, [i]but[/i] some choices affect later chapters, so the process of getting all possible outcomes is still tedious. The excessive achievements seem like a means of getting players to replay the game more than necessary and boost gameplay times. 
I also didn’t feel any attachment to the characters. A challenge of short stories like these is getting the reader to resonate with characters while still keeping things concise. I just feel like they weren’t built up enough. 

If you feel like none of what I’ve complained of would bother you, then sure, go for it. The stories themselves are interesting enough. But otherwise, I just can’t recommend it.

One of the best visual novels I've ever seen, and definitely the best point-and-click game I've played in a long time. Playing this and replaying it just to experience all the different choices, outcomes and endings has been an absolute joy.

While this game doesn't offer many puzzles, and the stories are all short and sweet, the connections between the stories that cause them to interweave with each other are what really make this game shine. The way the final episode provides historical context to the other three is particularly brilliant, making the characters feel almost real in a sense.

Because the events of each episode change slightly based on choices you make in the other episodes, you could easily replay this game a dozen times and find something new each time! It is worth noting, however, that the lack of achievements does limit replayability on the Switch version. An in-game equivalent system would fix this.

The graphics, audio, and overall UI of the game also provide this wonderfully artsy feel to everything, making the game feel especially charming and beautiful, kinda like a little window into the 1910s. Together, they create a wonderful aesthetic that really suits the story and characters, which makes it really easy to stay engaged.

So to reiterate, if you enjoy visual novels, point-and-click adventures, or even if you just want to experience an interesting story, I can't recommend this title enough!
